body-composition.short: What the body is made of: usually split into fat and everything else (muscle, bone, water, organs).

fat-mass.short: The mass of all the fat in the body, under the skin and around the organs, in kg.

fat-free-mass.short: Everything in the body that isn't fat: muscle, bone, organs and water. Lean mass is almost the same thing (it leaves out bone mineral).

two-compartment-model.short: Treating the body as just two parts, fat mass and fat-free mass, each with a fixed density. Measure one and the other is body mass minus it.

body-density.short: Body mass divided by body volume, in g·mL⁻¹. Fat is less dense (about 0.9) than fat-free mass (about 1.1), so a leaner body is denser.

hydrostatic-weighing.short: Weighing a person fully under water after breathing out. The weight lost in water gives body volume (Archimedes), and so body density.

air-displacement-plethysmography.short: Measuring body volume from how much air a person pushes out of a closed pod (the BOD POD), then body density, like underwater weighing but dry.

dxa.short: A low-dose X-ray scan at two energies. Bone, fat and lean tissue block the beams differently, so it maps all three, region by region.

bone-mineral-density.short: The amount of mineral (mostly calcium) per area of bone, measured by DXA, in g·cm⁻². Low BMD means weaker bones.

bia.short: Sending a tiny electric current through the body (as in body-fat scales). Water conducts it, so resistance gives body water, and equations turn that into fat-free mass.

skinfold.short: A double fold of skin and the fat just under it, pinched and measured in mm with calipers at set body sites.

accuracy.short: How close a measurement is to the true value. A scale that always reads 2 kg high is precise but not accurate.

precision.short: How close repeated measurements are to each other when nothing has changed. Shown by the typical error. It is what you need to track change.

rolling-resistance.short: The force lost as tyres squash and recover on the road. It grows with total weight; the coefficient Crr is about 0.003–0.006 on good roads.

frontal-area.short: The area of rider and bike seen from the front, in m², as the wind sees it.

cda.short: Frontal area times the drag coefficient (how smoothly air flows round the shape), in m². It sets how much force air resistance takes at a given speed.

allometric-scaling.short: Dividing a measure by body mass raised to a power (mass^b, e.g. W·kg⁻⁰·³²) instead of by mass itself, because the measure doesn't grow one-to-one with mass.

body-weight.short: The pull of gravity on your mass: a force, in newtons (mass × 9.81). In everyday speech 'weight' means mass in kg.

periodisation.short: Planning training (or diet, or body mass) in phases across the year, so each peaks when it matters instead of being held at one level all year.

low-energy-availability.short: Too little energy left for the body's own work after training is paid for. Short, mild spells can be harmless; long or severe ones cause REDs.

bone-stress-injury.short: Damage from repeated loading that bone can't repair fast enough: from a stress reaction (swelling inside the bone) up to a stress fracture.

amenorrhoea.short: Missing periods for 3 months or more. In athletes it is often a sign that the body is short of energy and has turned down its sex hormones.

female-athlete-triad.short: The older name for three linked problems in active women: low energy availability, menstrual problems and low bone density. REDs widened it to men and to more body systems.

z-score.short: How many standard deviations a result sits from the average of people of the same age and sex. A BMD Z-score of −1 is one SD below average.

bmi.short: Body mass in kg divided by height in metres squared (kg·m⁻²). A rough size measure: it can't tell muscle from fat.

dietary-restraint.short: Consciously holding back on food to control body weight, measured with questionnaires.
